cards.title: One field-write door: every contact write logs its revision and restamps its flags

cards.body:
## Summary
The four stored defect flags (phone_ok, is_stale, conflict, in_open_pair) are caches of four rules, and every write path restamps the ones it remembers by hand. Route every contact field write through one door in a new lib/flags.ts that records the revision, applies the value and restamps exactly the flags that field feeds; add flagDrift(), an oracle that recomputes every flag from its rule and reports any row where the cache disagrees; pin it under a seeded random walk of every mutation and undo.

## Description
The pattern is read-models-and-projections (data-access): a stored count is a cache, and a cache needs the rule it caches beside it plus a check. Today phone_ok is restamped in three places (mutations.ts:159, :387, :540), is_stale in one that arrived only after a bug (b135dbb4), conflict through refreshConflict which a fix had to correct (7e9209d2), and in_open_pair both derived (refreshPairFlag) and zeroed inline (:394, :429). The class has already produced two shipped defects. The audit half is write-chokepoint (audit-logging): merge is the one write that changes field values without a revisions row (:385), so the survivor's phone silently becomes the drop's. Through the door, a merge adoption writes a revision tagged merge_contacts, which exportSummary excludes from the normalised figures exactly as it excludes resolve_company.

## Flow
- lib/flags.ts: deriveFlags(row, ctx) and restamp(tx, {ids, domains}) - the only writer of the four flags; seed() stamps through deriveFlags too
- writeField(tx, id, field, value, rule) -> INSERT revision, UPDATE field, restamp what the field feeds; restoreField for applyUndo
- normalizeFields, resolveCompany, mergeContacts (adoptions), applyUndo call the door; deleteContacts and merge's merged_into/deleted_at writes call restamp
- flagDrift(): recompute over the working list, return [{id, flag, stored, derived}]
- test/flag-drift.test.ts: corruption detection + seeded random walk

## Expected impact
A new write path cannot forget a flag, and if one ever does the drift oracle names the row and the flag in the test run instead of a reviewer finding a stuck segment count. The survivor of a merge carries the history of what the merge changed on it. Could break: the sheet's 'changed' figure now counts merge adoptions on the survivor (correct, but visible); campaign.test.ts summary figures must stay put, which case 5 pins. Interacts with this host's slot B card in mergeContacts; whichever lands second rebases onto the door.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stored flags provably equal their rules after any sequence of writes, and every field write leaves a revision
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass as written (flagDrift and lib/flags.ts do not exist; merge writes no revision); 4 flag-writing sites outside any single module (grep)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: preview_merge shows what the irreversible merge will write, from the write's planner
shared_surfaces: examples/tidycrm/components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx (optional one-line description update for preview_merge; owned by tidycrm-spatial-model-tools - the card works without it because the tool returns the preview object verbatim)
acceptance: previewMergeAction(pair) where keep.phone_ok=0 and drop.phone_ok=1 -> result.outcome.adopts contains {field:'phone', from: keep.phone, to: drop.phone}; where drop.last_activity_at is newer -> contains the last_activity_at adoption

a pair whose drop stands in a second open pair -> outcome.closes lists that second pair's id; after mergeAction the second pair's status is 'skipped' and the set of pairs that changed status equals {settled pair} + outcome.closes

a pair whose drop holds its domain's last odd company spelling -> outcome.restamps contains {flag:'conflict', domain, from:1, to:0}; a drop newer than the stale cutoff on a stale keep -> {flag:'is_stale', id:keep_id, from:1, to:0}

parity walk: for the first 10 open pairs in turn, plan then merge -> the survivor's stored phone, last_activity_at, phone_ok and is_stale equal outcome.survivor field for field, and countSegment('all') drops by exactly 1 each time
preview of a pair whose drop was merged by an earlier pair -> outcome.refusal is the exact error string mergeContacts returns for the same ids, and outcome.adopts/closes are empty
previewMergeAction still returns pair, keep, drop and conflicts with the same values as before (existing callers and the preview_merge tool keep their fields)
mergeContacts' refusals and activity summary text are unchanged for the seed's first pair

examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:340 adoptions() decides what the survivor takes, and nothing outside mergeContacts calls it
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:397 closeDependentPairs silently closes every other open pair the drop stood in
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:400 refreshConflict may clear the drop's domain from the conflicts segment
examples/tidycrm/lib/db.ts:350 previewPair returns the two rows and their disagreements only - no adoption, no closed pair, no flag change
examples/tidycrm/app/actions.ts:116 previewMergeAction is previewPair verbatim; it is what the preview_merge tool returns (components/shell/HostCapabilities.tsx:285)
examples/tidycrm/lib/mutations.ts:125 and :257 planNormalize and planCompany already follow plan-then-write from one planner; merge is the only write without one
cards.rollback: Two commits (planMerge + outcome on the preview; mergeContacts executing the plan), reverted in reverse order; the outcome field is additive, so reverting the first leaves every existing caller's fields intact.

cards.body:
## Summary
The only irreversible, gated act in TidyCRM is approved blind. preview_merge shows the two records and where they disagree, but not what the merge will do: which values the survivor takes, which other open pairs it closes as skipped, which flags and segments it clears. The app computes all of it - inside mergeContacts, after the approval. Extract planMerge(keep, drop) as the single planner both the preview and the write run, and attach its outcome to the preview.

## Description
This is blast-radius-computation (entity-lifecycle): the preview and the execution share one implementation, and the consequences are enumerated before the ask. planNormalize and planCompany already follow plan-then-write; merge is the one write that does not, and it is the irreversible one. outcome carries {refusal?, adopts[], closes[], restamps[], survivor}. mergeContacts becomes: plan, refuse with plan.refusal, apply plan. Because the preview_merge tool returns the preview object as is, the agent and the person reading the approval card see the outcome without a tool change. The gate class is untouched (merge stays reversible:false, GATED, per ADR 0004).

## Flow
- read_pairs -> pair_007
- preview_merge(pair_007) -> conflicts as today + outcome: 'survivor takes phone +14155550134 and last activity 2026-03-02; closes pair_031 (skipped); clears acme.example from Company conflicts; survivor no longer stale'
- the person approves the merge card knowing what it writes -> merge_contacts executes that exact plan
- if anything moved between preview and approval, the write re-plans and the refusal is the planner's own string

## Expected impact
The reviewer approving an irreversible merge sees its consequences, including the silent closure of other pairs that today is discovered only as a vanished queue entry. A whole class of preview/write drift closes because there is one planner. Could break: callers that deep-equal the preview object (case 6 pins the existing fields). Shares mergeContacts with this host's slot A card; whichever lands second rebases.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the merge preview states what the merge will write, and the write does exactly that
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass as written (no outcome field; adopts/closes/restamps computed only inside the write)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence:
lib/db.ts:350-357 previewPair -> { pair, keep, drop, conflicts: conflictsBetween(keep, drop) } - nothing else.
lib/mutations.ts:382 `const taken = adoptions(keep, drop);` computed after the precondition checks, inside the gated write; :397 `closeDependentPairs(tx, drop.id);` closes other open pairs as 'skipped'; :400 `refreshConflict(tx, drop.domain);`.
HostCapabilities.tsx:285-287 preview_merge handler: `const preview = await previewMergeAction(String(pair_id)); return preview ?? ...` - returns the object verbatim, so an added field reaches the agent.

rehomed: Actor provenance - every write logs actor 'user' even when Athena made it (stabilize backlog, L): the fix carries caller identity from the WebMCP transport through demo-kit and every app, outside this host's write set.

Reversible merge/delete via snapshot inverses: flipping the manifest's reversible flag would reclassify the tools AUTO under ADR 0004 - a policy loosen; keeping them GATED but undoable is a direction call for the deck.
Bulk-merge every confident pair in one gated act: one card authorising up to 43 irreversible merges weakens per-act consent - policy-loosen risk.
Export summary counts tidies on records since deleted (stabilize backlog): S, effort 2, gate direction.
Context description names 'CSV import' but no import exists (registry: import-normalization not-applicable): building one is a direction, not a fix.
